Ubuntu Cultural Conversations
The Undercurrent presents Ubuntu Cultural Conversations!

The Ubuntu Cultural Conversation is an interactive and inclusive cultural event that explores how humanity is understood, expressed, preserved, and shared through diverse cultural perspectives. Through a combination of live music, poetry, storytelling, and open audience conversations, the event will create a space for meaningful dialogue, cultural exchange, reflection, and connection.

The programme will feature live musical performances by Ras Judah (Botswana), Mohamed Shemi (Tanzania), and friends, alongside poetry and opportunities for audience participation. Shared cultural food will further contribute to the spirit of hospitality, community, and connection that lies at the heart of Ubuntu.

The African concept of Ubuntu is often expressed through the powerful saying, “I am because we are.” Rather than placing individual achievement at the centre of social life, Ubuntu emphasises the importance of community, cooperation, reciprocity, and shared wellbeing. It encourages us to recognise the humanity in one another and to respond to the challenges faced by others with understanding, kindness, and support.

The philosophy of Ubuntu reminds us that our lives are enriched when we care for one another, celebrate our differences, and work collectively to create inclusive and connected communities. It offers an opportunity to reflect on what it means to be human and how our relationships with others shape the societies in which we live.

Techno Echo: Fox Moss
Techno Echo is a meet-up for women and gender minorities to learn and share about audio and visual practices and technology. Featuring special micro performances and demonstrations by local artists/musicians followed by time for kōrero and connection.

Our guest artist Fox Moss is the solo musical project of Te Whanganui-a-Tara based multidisciplinary musician and artist Niamh Woollin. Fox Moss released her debut album: Eternal Veil in September 2026. The album explores ambient and dungeon synth genres, with an overarching narrative structuring the album. Fox Moss creates and performs using Ableton, conjuring her immersive experiences through layering electronic sounds and textures. Niamh creates all the visual elements to accompany her music.

Introduced to Wellington’s music scene through their band Maiden Name in 2023, Niamh began making music under Fox Moss in 2024 after releasing her first single In Between. Fox Moss first performed at 13 Garrett Street for Attic Sessions #001 in April 2025. She released her second single, A Thousand White Horses soon after. In early 2026 Niamh performed at POWER2PONEKE and TONIC002: Insula x Niph.

Tumunu Writers Gathering | Breaking Ground Festival
Join us at Hannah Playhouse at this whakawhanaungatanga event for our creative hapori. This will be a chance to catch up, get to know other writers, and enjoy a relaxed quiz night.

Tumunu is a free event and is part of our wider schedule of public events for Breaking Ground.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

Check out our other events here:

The Chapel of Our Lady of Compassion Tour
Join a tour of our Category 1 Historic Place Chapel and Resting Place of Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert. Come experience the rich history of this sacred space.

Two forty-five-minute tours will be offered over the course of each morning. Each tour will include the history of the building, the meanings behind the stained-glass windows, and the significance of the site as an ongoing place of worship. Participants will have the opportunity to visit the final Resting Place of Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert who founded the Sisters of Compassion, the only religious order born in Aotearoa New Zealand. Come and experience the rich history and spirituality that are embedded in these sacred places.

Our Cloister Cafe will be open to welcome you for coffee or lunch. Please stick around after your tour and enjoy the cafe and grounds!

Live Reading | New Pages: Mate by Regan Taylor
Join us for this live reading of a new script in development by Regan Taylor.

New Pages intentionally carves out space for the earliest phase of the creative process, inviting you into the room when characters and concepts are still fluid and shifting. It captures the essence of trusting the story before completely understanding it.

Mate is the new work-in-development by writer Regan Taylor (Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Pikiao), a Wellington-based theatre maker, director, actor, tutor, writer, occasional troublemaker and all-round theatre lover.

Regan is a graduate of the UCOL Theatre School, he's been making, directing, performing and teaching theatre across Aotearoa and Australia for the past 25 years. He's a regular director for Taki Rua and their Te Reo Māori seasons and Toi Whakaari – New Zealand Drama School, and is a founding member of Te Rēhia Theatre in Auckland. Next up, Regan is making a new touring show with The Māori Sidesteps, releasing Resilience, the latest children's album with The KaRs, and getting stuck into writing.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010.

Check out the full schedule here:
https://tawataproductions.com/breaking-ground/

Mate is presented from 7.30PM Friday November 20 2026 at the Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Tce, Te Aro, Wellington.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

Same Name Confusion are embarking on a trans-Tasman tour in support of their new album, SNC (out September 25 via Winegum Records).

Silver Clay Taster - November
Join us in our warm and friendly studio to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Silver Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants, earrings or charms. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Silver Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant, earrings, or a couple of charms.

A discussion of 'The Origins of an Experimental Society – New Zealand 1769 – 1860' by Erik Olssen, Auckland University Press, 2025.

Associate Professors Annabel Cooper and Malcolm McKinnon will reflect on Professor Olssen’s work and its enduring significance.

Professor Olssen died in July at the age of 84, and this event will be a tribute to his last book and a lifetime of research into New Zealand history.

About this Event


Executive Briefing for CIOs, Strategy, Digital and Transformation Leaders



AI, transformation, cyber resilience and cost optimisation continue to dominate executive agendas, yet many organisations still lack a connected view of how these priorities impact the broader enterprise.

Join Kapish and Ardoq for an executive briefing exploring how leading organisations are making better decisions through greater visibility across strategy, business capabilities, technology, risk and investment.

Using a fictional organisation facing familiar business challenges, our consultants will walk through a series of executive scenarios involving transformation, AI adoption, technology risk, application rationalisation and operational resilience. We'll demonstrate how leaders can better understand impacts, dependencies and risk through a connected enterprise view enabled by Ardoq.

You'll gain practical insights into how organisations are:

Understanding the impact of strategic and technology decisions
Identifying hidden dependencies and risks
Reducing complexity and unnecessary duplication
Prioritising transformation and technology investments
Strengthening governance for AI and business change

The session includes practical use cases, a live demonstration of the scenarios within Ardoq, and opportunities for questions with our consultants and enterprise architecture specialists.

long_description:
Eco Dye Workshop
Impressions of Nature on Silk

Eco dyeing, also known as leaf or eco print, is a gentle, alchemical process where the natural pigments of leaves are transferred directly onto fabric, creating one-of-a-kind botanical imprints.

Join me for a full day of slow making and discovery as we explore this beautiful dialogue between nature and cloth. In the morning, we’ll forage around the hall, gathering leaves and foliage that speak to us. You’ll learn how to prepare and bundle silk with plant materials, drawing out colours and patterns from the landscape itself.

In the afternoon, you’ll design and dye your own silk scarf — a wearable memory of place and season, marked by the delicate traces of nature’s touch.

You will learn

• which plants and fibres work best for this method
• how to use an iron mordant to enhance colour and detail
• different bundling techniques and approaches

All materials and tools will be provided for use during the workshop.

Your workshop fee includes silk fabrics to explore and experiment with, one silk scarf to design and dye, and a detailed handout with information on mordants, dye plants, tips, and useful resources.

A ‘what to bring’ list (including suggestions for clothing and optional items) will be sent out closer to the workshop date.

Booking through my website (see link above)

Location

27A Elizabeth Street (Art and Craft Society)
Waikane
Kāpiti

long_description:
Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level
Spend your Sunday mornings immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It runs from Sun 1 November for 4 weeks till Sun 22 November, 10am-1pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These Sunday sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up. Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Course fee $250, Early bird $225 till 5 October.

Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.

The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.

After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.

This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".

Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.

Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

Korimako Trio playing at the Martinborough Town Hall, Sept 8 at 4.00pm

For their first visit to Martinborough the Korimako Trio have a wonderful programme to share with you that combines classical elegance with romantic depth, a programme which showcases the warmth and deeply communicative musicianship of these star performers.
The concert opens with Zemlinsky's Trio in D Minor, a late 19th century example of Viennese Romanticism, lyrical, dense and emotionally expressive. This is followed by Janacek’s Violin Sonata (for violin and piano) deeply dramatic with folk elements. A return to Romanticism with Chopin’s Introduction and Polonaise Brillante in C major, for cello and piano follows and the concert concludes with Haydn’s Piano trio in A major (Hob.XV), bright and witty, with plenty of classical charm. A beautifully varied journey through four distinct musical eras, balancing full trio textures with virtuoso duo highlights.

November 8 at 4.00pm
Martinborough Town Hall

IP for SaaS - How to Protect Your Business
A practical session for SaaS founders on IP, ownership and protecting what you’re building.

About this Event



Your code, your product name, your brand, that clever bit of workflow you’re quietly proud of. It’s all IP, and most founders don’t think about it until someone else is using it. Savvy businesses protect their IP with trade secrets, trade marks, copyright and more.

Spend an afternoon with the team from IPONZ, alongside other founders asking the same questions. Leave knowing what you own, what you don’t, and what to do next.

Afternoon tea is provided from 3:30pm, with the event starting at 4pm. Stay afterwards for networking drinks with the experts and other founders.

The IPONZ experts -

Alicia Baxter is Principal Business Advisor (IP Strategy) at IPONZ, working across NZ's commercialisation ecosystem where she focuses on driving early engagement to make sure the value of IP is understood upfront, not after the fact. With a BSc(Hons) in Chemistry from the University of Auckland and a double major in chemistry and genetics from Massey University, Alicia joined IPONZ in 2021 as a patent examiner and progressed to Senior Patent Examiner before moving into business-facing roles, including Business Advisor at MBIE and Business Lead at IPONZ. Alicia is passionate about positioning IP as a core business asset and helping innovators turn great ideas into commercial outcomes.

Jeanette Singh is a Principal Trade Mark Examiner at IPONZ with more than 25 years’ experience in intellectual property law across the public and private sectors. She began her career at IPONZ before spending more than 15 years at Bell Gully, where she progressed to Senior Associate and advised across trade marks, copyright, designs and broader IP matters. Her experience includes drafting commercial IP contracts, leading IP due diligence projects and providing franchising advice. Jeanette has also run her own IP practice advising start-ups. While her expertise spans intellectual property, her particular passion is trade marks and the way this area continues to evolve.

Dr Penny Walsh delivers core IP services for IPONZ and is passionate about making intellectual property easier to understand and use. With a PhD in Chemistry and a background as a registered New Zealand patent attorney, Penny brings a strong combination of scientific and practical IP expertise. She has worked with clients across a wide range of industries to protect and manage their intellectual property, with experience spanning patents, trade marks, copyright and broader IP issues. Penny particularly enjoys contributing to IP education and helping people build the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their intellectual property.

Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

* The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

* the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

* Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

* Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

* Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.



SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.



THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.



YOUR TEACHER

[ ]

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.



YOUR HOSTS

Sarah and Liz [ ]

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community.



FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

Live Reading | On The Edge: The Boy From Vaiala by Victor Rodger
In this intimate session, we hold space for a live, raw reading of a vital new play in development. This is your invitation to sit beside the flame of creation before the ink is fully dry.

We welcome our community, arts audiences, and potential venue and festival partners to witness this latest work, and celebrate new Indigenous scriptwriting in development.

The Boy From Vaiala is the new work-in-development by award-winning playwright and producer Victor Rodger (Samoa (Iva), Scotland (Broughty Ferry)). Known for his bold and provocative works that delve into race, identity, and sexuality, Victor is a graduate of Toi Whakaari New Zealand Drama School.

Victor’s first play, Sons, premiered at The Court Theatre in Ōtautahi Christchurch. A revised version of Sons was subsequently produced by Taki Rua Productions, winning four Chapman Tripp Theatre Awards, including Most Outstanding New Writer and Most Outstanding New Zealand Play. Under his FCC banner, Victor has produced award winning productions of The Mountaintop by Katori Hall as well as Wild Dogs Under My Skirt and The Savage Coloniser Show by 2020 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate Tusiata Avia. The Boy From Vaiala will premiere at ASB Waterfront Theatre with Auckland Theatre Company in 2027.

The Boy From Vaiala is presented from 4PM Sunday November 22 2026 at the Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Tce, Te Aro, Wellington.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

long_description:
He Kōrerorero: A Conversation about Indigenous Dramaturgy (Writers Workshop)
He Kōrerorero is an ongoing conversation about the practice of Indigenous dramaturgy in Aotearoa and Te Whenua Moemoeā, Australia.

In conversation with award-winning writer, director and producer Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Kahungunu) and Birribay, Worrimay theatremaker and academic Dr.Liza-Mare Syron. He Kōrerorero will share insights into their dramaturgical practice of the development of new Indigenous writing. He Kōrerorero will workshop and discuss the evolution of Indigenous dramaturgy and share tools for managing this practice within the Indigenous arts sector today. Hone and Dr. Liza-Mare will include both playwriting and screenwriting as part of their discussions.

This workshop is relevant for scriptwriters, theatremakers, filmmakers, producers and developers who are working across both stage and screen.

A theatre maker and academic, Liza-Mare is an Associate Professor Scientia in the School of Arts and Media at UNSW and the Co-Associate Dean Indigenous in the Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture. As a founding member of Moogahlin Performing Arts, NSW’s leading Aboriginal Theatre company, Liza-Mare has directed, produced, and been a dramaturge of many award-winning productions such as The Visitors by Marrawarri playwright Jane Harrison and The Weekend by Kuku Yalanji playwright Henrietta Baird.

Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Kahungunu) is a father, a member of the New Zealand Order of Merit, an acclaimed Māori writer, producer and director, the youngest winner of the Bruce Mason Playwriting Award. In 2022, Hone was named an Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate, receiving the Sir Roger Hall Theatre Award. Hone’s plays include Ngā Tangata Toa, Waiora: Te Ūkaipō, The Prophet and Bless The Child. In 2004, Hone co-founded the production company, Tawata Productions, focusing on the development and presentation of new theatre by Māori and Pasifika artists. Hone is the co-founder of Kia Mau Festival.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

https://tawataproductions.com/breaking-ground/

He Kōrerorero is presented from 10AM-1PM Tuesday November 17 2026 at the Toi Aro, 3 Market Lane, Te Aro, Wellington.

There are only 12 spaces offered for this workshop.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Toi Aro, Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.
